LAYOUT SPEC for evergreen_spec_card_2024.pdf — render as a genuine press PDF from a full layout engine with embedded font subsets (NOT a thin hand-authored PDF). One page, the decorator's own spec-card format from last season, roughly 8.5 x 11 in portrait. NO bleed.

CRITICAL STRUCTURE (planted trap, author exactly): the FOUR blocks below read as visually separate on the printed page, but they must be set as ONE continuous text story in ONE text frame (running lines with breaks between blocks), NOT four frames. The frame granularity the conversion exposes will therefore be nothing like the printed page suggests.

VISIBLE BLOCKS (top to bottom, all one story):
  Block 1 — JOB header: 'JOB: ____  ·  GARMENT: ____  ·  COLOUR: ____'
  Block 2 — INK LIST: 'INKS (in order): 1) ____  2) ____  3) ____  4) ____'
  Block 3 — PLATE ORDER: 'PLATE ORDER / SCREENS: ____ then ____ then ____'
  Block 4 — PLACEMENT: 'PLACEMENT: ____  ·  PRINT WIDTH: ____ in  ·  UNDERBASE: ____'

Field labels the merge targets: JOB, GARMENT, COLOUR, INK_LIST, PLATE_ORDER, PLACEMENT, PRINT_WIDTH, UNDERBASE. Sample values are last season's, e.g. JOB 'Deschutes Tote', GARMENT 'Tote', COLOUR 'Natural', INKS '1) Cedar Bark 2) Sage', PLATE ORDER 'Sage then Cedar Bark', PLACEMENT 'Centre', PRINT WIDTH '9', UNDERBASE 'none'. Plain workhorse sans, a decorator's utilitarian card, cedar-ink (#1A1714) type on bone (#E7E0D0).
assets.defect_engineered: the four visibly separate blocks are one continuous flow (frame granularity unlike the printed page), and the readout will drop one run while keeping its line break so offsets past it go short and the validator still reports valid

assets.content:
INK BOOK — what the decorator keeps on the shelf (anything off this list is a mixing charge)

Standard plastisols we always have:
- Bench Black (dense black)
- Bone Primer (natural off-white, good underbase on darks)
- Cedar Bark (warm mid-brown)
- Sage Field (muted grey-green)
- Aubergine Deep (dark purple-brown) — low stock, tell us early
- Harvest Gold (warm ochre)

Shop notes:
- On black and the black hoodie we usually lay a Bone Primer underbase or nothing prints bright. Underbase counts as a screen and a pass.
- Sage over Cedar Bark is our favourite two-colour combo, it reads hand-painted.
- Aubergine is a pain, it is thin and it sits close to a stained-wood look, do not put it on the olive.
- Halftones: we can hold a coarse dot for a paint-field look. Keep the smallest dot open, fine dots plug on the fleece.
- Every extra screen is real money on a short run. If a design is worth two inks not three, say so.

We like: earthy, few colours, the brush showing. We do not want: neon, foil, or anything that looks like gas-station merch.
assets.defect_engineered: none (clean support asset: the stock inks map to the brand palette and gate the reduction, and the notes name the underbase-as-a-screen cost, the aubergine limitation and the coarse-dot-only halftone that drive the ink-count decisions)
